diagnostic_evidence.quote: In the present work, we consider fluctuations that are derived by taking the linear path $\Phi(s) = \bB{u}^- + s \jump{\bB{u}}$ and approximating the path integral in \eqref{eq:path_conservation_cond} with the trapezoidal rule to obtain

issues.failure_explanation: The matrix B is not affine along a straight path in conservative variables because it contains u_m=(hu_m)/h and analogous moment ratios. For the one-moment SWLME, take (h,hu_m,hα_1)^-=(1,0,0) and (h,hu_m,hα_1)^+=(2,2,2), with constant bottom. Along the prescribed path, u_m(s)=2s/(1+s). The exact nonconservative moment integral is −4(1−log 2), whereas the fluctuations use −avg(u_m)[[hα_1]]=−1. Thus their sum does not satisfy the stated path-conservation equality.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Describe these fluctuations as a quadrature approximation rather than an exactly path-conservative discretization of the specified path, and withdraw any inference of exact shock jump consistency with that path. The entropy and lake-at-rest claims can be retained independently.
issues.overall_effect: Exact conservation for the prescribed straight path, and the corresponding interpretation of finite discontinuities, are unsupported. The separately derived two-point entropy identity does not eliminate this path-integral discrepancy.
issues.title: Trapezoidal fluctuations fail the declared straight-path conservation condition
issues.why_classification: The discrepancy persists at finite jumps, so it is not a harmless quadrature error removed by ordinary mesh refinement across a shock. A limited weakening preserves the main entropy-stability and well-balancing framework but loses a substantive path-consistency guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: The pure-SWE zero-potential identity is applied using the full SWME entropy vector. Its SWE contribution is actually −avg(hu_m) Σ_j avg(α_j)[[α_j]]/(2j+1), not zero. For h=u_m=1, constant bottom, and α_1 changing from 0 to 1, it equals −1/6. The subsequent expansion of the remaining linear-moment contribution omits the opposite +1/6 term. Those terms cancel only when the contributions are combined; the two separate equalities used in the proof are false.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain the nonzero SWE residual and combine the SWE and linear-moment contributions before applying the jump product rule. Its cancellation with the corresponding moment-flux term then gives the stated potential jump.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's hierarchical proof uses an invalid premise. The complete numerical flux can nevertheless satisfy the claimed entropy identity.
issues.title: The EC-flux proof incorrectly discards the SWE contribution for full moment entropy variables
issues.why_classification: This is a local regrouping of terms already present in the source. It requires neither a new flux nor a new lemma and preserves the substantive theorem and numerical guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: with vectors $\mbf{y} = (1, u_m, \bB{\alpha}^{\rm T})^{\rm T}$ and $\mbf{z} = (1, gh, 3gh, \dots, (2n+1)gh)^{\rm T}$ is the positive definite inverse of the Hessian

issues.failure_explanation: At zero velocity and moments, the inverse Hessian of the displayed energy has diagonal entries (1/g,h,3h,...), but the proposed matrix has height entry 2/g because both yy^T and diag(z) contribute 1 there. Consequently, for constant bottom and resting states with h^-=1 and h^+=2, the height component of diag(Hbar,1)[[w]] is 2 rather than [[h]]=1. Both the inverse-Hessian identification and the claimed finite-jump relation fail.

failure_location.quote: that for  constant bottom topography satisfies the relation $\text{diag}(\bar{\mbf{H}}, 1) \jump{\bB{w}} = \jump{\bB{u}}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the first component of z by 0. The resulting matrix has the correct inverse-Hessian form and satisfies the constant-bottom jump relation.
issues.overall_effect: The stated conversion between entropy-variable and conservative-variable Rusanov dissipation is incorrect. This defect does not itself destroy positive definiteness or the sign of the entropy-dissipation quadratic form.
issues.title: The dissipation metric fails its inverse-Hessian and finite-jump identities
issues.why_classification: A short local correction restores the claimed algebraic identities while preserving positive definiteness, entropy dissipation, and well-balancing.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: with vectors $\mbf{y} = (1, u_m, \bB{\alpha}^{\rm T})^{\rm T}$ and $\mbf{z} = (1, gh, 3gh, \dots, (2n+1)gh)^{\rm T}$

issues.failure_explanation: This assertion fails independently of the erroneous height-diagonal entry. Take zero moments, constant bottom, and conservative endpoints (h,hu_m)^-=(1,1), (h,hu_m)^+=(2,1). The matrix's off-diagonal and momentum-diagonal entries force an inverse-Hessian evaluation state with u_m=3/4 and h=3/2, hence hu_m=9/8. Every state on the conservative-variable segment has hu_m=1. Thus even the correctly normalized matrix has no such segment-state representation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Identify the evaluation state explicitly by arithmetic primitive means: h=avg(h), u_m=avg(u_m), and α=avg(α). Do not assert that its conservative representation lies on the straight conservative-state segment; use avg(h)>0 to establish admissibility.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted intermediate-state characterization is false and cannot serve as a justification of the metric's properties.
issues.title: Primitive averaging does not produce an intermediate conservative-segment state
issues.why_classification: The required state identification is routine and local. It changes no numerical flux or dissipation matrix and preserves the properties needed by the entropy argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where the unscaled coefficients are $\widetilde{A}_{ijk}\coloneqq A_{ijk}/(2i+1)$ and $\widetilde{B}_{ijk} \coloneqq B_{ijk}/(2i+1)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The cited identity concerns normalized tensors. It implies A_{kji}=−((2k+1)/(2i+1) B_{ijk}+B_{kji}), not the prescribed unweighted sum. For N=2, the supplied polynomial definitions give B_{112}=1/5 and B_{211}=−1. The algorithm therefore returns A_{211}=4/5, whereas its defining integral gives 2/3.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use A_{kji}=−((2k+1)/(2i+1) B_{ijk}+B_{kji}), or perform the reconstruction on normalized tensors and then rescale. Recompute and verify any numerical output produced using the unweighted rule.
issues.overall_effect: Computations following this recipe do not instantiate the defined SWME tensors and cannot invoke the coefficient identity underlying the energy and EC analyses. The formal results for the exact integral-defined tensors are not themselves refuted.
issues.title: Tensor reconstruction drops the Legendre normalization factors
issues.why_classification: The source already supplies the exact identity needed for a local normalization correction. No new construction, proof architecture, or loss of the intended method and guarantees is required.
